A secret to sustainable recovery: Integrate Peacebuilding into Humanitarian and Development Work

Dr. Kyi Minn explains that in conflict situations, a triple response following humanitarian emergencies is vital. 

Theoretically, in any humanitarian situation, the provision of aid is crucial as the first step in responding to the immediate needs of affected communities, and development work follows to ensure sustained recovery, rehabilitation, and development. But this is not necessarily the best model in every context. 

Looking back at my personal experience leading humanitarian response operations for World Vision in Myanmar after Cyclone Nargis in 2008, I saw our teams following this model, starting with humanitarian assistance supporting the populations affected by the cyclone, and then transitioning to development programmes aimed at fostering long-term growth and self-sufficiency. In most cases, the model works. However, the ongoing conflict in Myanmar, one of the world's longest-running protracted crisis, highlights the limitations of this approach in complex humanitarian contexts. 

This underscores a vital truth: sustainable development cannot be achieved without peace. What I quickly realised was that the double nexus of humanitarian aid, followed by development, is grossly insufficient in conflict-ridden areas. This reality demands change: an integration of peacebuilding into humanitarian and development efforts – creating a triple nexus approach. Peace is not just a desirable outcome; it is the necessary precondition for our humanitarian and development initiatives to succeed. 

Peacebuilding is challenging, but a must

Firstly, it allows for the exchange of ideas and expertise, leading to innovative solutions and approaches.

Environmental challenges are multifaceted, and a diverse team can provide fresh perspectives and alternative solutions.

Moreover, collaboration fosters a holistic approach to problem-solving.

By combining knowledge from different disciplines, environmental engineers can consider all aspects of a project, including ecological, social, and economic factors.

This comprehensive approach leads to more sustainable and balanced outcomes that meet the needs of both nature and society.

Working together as a team also enhances communication and understanding among professionals.

Each discipline brings its own technical jargon and methodologies, but through collaboration, these barriers are broken down.

Effective communication ensures that all stakeholders are on the same page, reducing misunderstandings and facilitating a seamless workflow.

In fact, collaboration between environmental engineers and other professionals is essential for effective nature preservation.

By working hand-in-hand with biologists, archaeologists, and policy-makers, environmental engineers can harness the full potential of interdisciplinary expertise.

Together, they can develop comprehensive and sustainable solutions that safeguard Canada’s precious natural resources for future generations.

Success Stories

The Great Lakes Remedial Action Plan

Environmental engineers played a crucial role in restoring and preserving the Great Lakes, one of Canada’s most important natural resources.

Through innovative engineering solutions, they successfully tackled issues like industrial pollution, sewage contamination, and habitat degradation.

As a result, the water quality in the Great Lakes has significantly improved, benefiting aquatic life, drinking water sources, and recreational activities.

The remediation efforts have also contributed to the revitalization of local communities, promoting tourism and economic growth along the lakefront.

Coastal Erosion Mitigation

Engineers developed sustainable strategies to combat erosion along Canada’s coastlines, protecting valuable ecosystems and infrastructure.

Through the use of innovative materials, like permeable barriers and artificial reefs, they have reduced the impact of erosion on vulnerable shorelines.

These projects have not only safeguarded coastal habitats but have also preserved important cultural sites and coastal communities.

Urban Green Building Initiatives

Environmental engineers have been instrumental in promoting sustainable development practices in Canadian cities.

They have designed energy-efficient buildings, implemented green infrastructure systems, and encouraged the use of renewable energy sources.

These initiatives have resulted in reduced carbon emissions, improved air quality, and enhanced urban biodiversity.

Additionally, the integration of green spaces in urban areas has provided residents with access to natural environments, contributing to their overall well-being.

In 2017, the EU and NATO added further areas of joint work for a total of 74 actions. The overwhelming majority of the actions have a long-term perspective requiring continued implementation since they represent recurring processes which continually produce gradual results, rather than single one-off events. However, a process of continuous engagement has been established and, according to the Third progress report on the implementation of the common set of proposals endorsed by NATO and EU Councils, the EU Hybrid Fusion Cell, the NATO Hybrid Analysis Branch and the European Centre of Excellence for Countering Hybrid Threats are all in frequent contact with each other and have developed strong working relationships. On situational awareness, staff-to-staff discussions between respective geographical and thematic clusters of the EU's Single Intelligence Analysis Capacity and NATO's Joint Intelligence and Security Division have been established and the EU Hybrid Fusion Cell and the NATO Hybrid Analysis Branch are also able to communicate via the EU version of the NATO Battlefield Information Collection and Exploitation System (BICES). Furthermore, regular strategic foresight discussions between NATO and EU staff has taken place. The Centre of Excellence effectively contributes to strengthening EU-NATO cooperation in the area of hybrid threats while formulating recommendations for further enhancing cooperation in the fields of early warning and situational awareness, strategic communication and messaging, crisis response, resilience, and cyber defence and energy security (European Council 2018).

EU-NATO cooperation, despite numerous historical frictions, is one formed out of necessity, imposed by the international environment, that could have many positive implications. A concrete development of European defence capabilities, avoiding unnecessary redundancies, is key in joint efforts to make the Euro-Atlantic area safer and contribute to transatlantic burden-sharing. In order to improve cooperation in the future, both organizations shall focus on deeper intelligence data exchange, strategic communication, development of coordinated procedures and security capacity building.

Mr. Thein Sein's subsequent appointment as President elicited no excitement inside or outside Myanmar. He had been the junta's prime minister, and was seen as a weak figure with no support, whether in the general population or the military.

Many believe that he was chosen precisely because of that weakness; he was supposedly a figure Gen. Than Shwe could easily manipulate as he continued to control the country from the shadows. Mr. Thein Sein would be the regime's slightly more pleasant face, but few believed anything substantive had changed in Naypyidaw, the junta's newly built and bizarrely empty capital city.

But then the unexpected happened: Gen. Than Shwe really did retire, or at least disappeared from the public eye. Some say he fell ill. And Mr. Thein Sein, whose reputation in the country was as a relatively moderate and uncorrupt general in a regime dominated by hardliners and kleptocrats, was suddenly in control.

Those who know Mr. Thein Sein say he grew disillusioned with the junta system after Cyclone Nargis in 2008, which saw his native Irrawaddy Delta obliterated and 130,000 people killed.

Though theoretically in charge of the relief operation, Mr. Thein Sein was hamstrung by his own bureaucracy and Gen. Than Shwe's refusal to allow in outside help. It's likely that tens of thousands of cyclone victims died unnecessarily because of the government's inept response.

After Nargis, a clique of would-be reformers (some of whom are now in Mr. Thein Sein's cabinet) began to develop inside the regime. Three years later, they found themselves in charge of the country.

“People mistakenly refer to the old system as the ‘junta,' when in fact it was a dictatorship of one man, Senior General Than Shwe. Integrated Communication Systems

Following Gedaliah’s death, chaos erupted. The remnants of the Jewish community found themselves in a dire situation, unsure of their next steps. Johanan immediately stepped in to provide guidance. He and the other leaders convened to decide the future of their people, which revealed his ability to think strategically in times of crisis.

Johanan proposed fleeing to Egypt to escape potential retribution from the Babylonians. This decision was met with mixed reactions. On one hand, it offered safety, but on the other, it meant abandoning their homeland. The people looked to Johanan for direction, highlighting his critical leadership role in navigating uncertainty.

Sadly, the decision to flee turned out to be a controversial one. God had warned against going to Egypt, leading to further complications as seen in Jeremiah 42. Despite Johanan’s intentions to protect his people, his actions had significant consequences, revealing the complexities of leadership in turbulent times.

Johanan the High Priest

Background and Significance

Another character named Johanan is the high priest who served during the post-exilic period of Jewish history. This Johanan is often associated with the important reforms that took place after the Babylonian exile. High priests played a crucial role in restoring and maintaining the worship practices of the Jewish people, especially as they rebuilt the Temple in Jerusalem.

Role in Rebuilding the Community

Johanan, as the high priest, had the responsibility of guiding the spiritual life of the Jewish nation. His leadership was vital during a time when the people sought to reconnect with their faith and traditions. Under his guidance, many reforms took place, reinstating the centrality of worship in Jewish life.

Ezra 10 records how Johanan witnessed the people confessing their sins and recommitting themselves to God. This act of repentance and renewal was pivotal in restoring hope and faith among the people. Johanan’s influence can also be seen during the time of Nehemiah, where he supported the efforts to rebuild Jerusalem’s walls, serving as a unifying figure during a crucial rebuilding period.

Spiritual Reforms and Legislative Actions

One of Johanan’s notable contributions was his involvement in enacting spiritual reforms. The Jewish community faced challenges in defining their identity post-exile. Johanan was instrumental in advocating for strict adherence to the Law of Moses and pushed for communal observance of religious festivals. This reform not only helped restore traditional practices but also reinforced the importance of a unified national identity centered around their faith.

Heritage preservation projects often involve navigating complex bureaucratic processes, including obtaining permits, approvals, and compliance with regulations. Consultants also assist in building resilience and adapting preservation strategies to changing circumstances.

Preservation of historic city centers

Heritage preservation consulting has been instrumental in the preservation of historic city centers around the world. Consultants work with local governments, businesses, and communities to develop preservation plans, enhance infrastructure, and protect the unique character of these urban areas. Through careful planning and implementation, historic city centers are revitalized and preserved for future generations to enjoy.

Restoration of iconic landmarks

Heritage preservation consultants have played a crucial role in restoring and preserving iconic landmarks, such as ancient temples, castles, and monuments. Adaptive reuse of heritage buildings

Heritage preservation consultants work with stakeholders to identify appropriate new uses for these buildings, while respecting their historical and architectural integrity. This can include converting a former factory into a museum or transforming an old school into residential units. Adaptive reuse projects breathe new life into heritage buildings, ensuring their continued relevance and sustainability.

Dealing with bureaucratic processes

Heritage preservation projects often involve navigating complex bureaucratic processes, including obtaining permits, approvals, and compliance with regulations. Heritage preservation consultants help stakeholders navigate these processes, ensuring that preservation projects meet legal requirements and obtain the necessary permissions. Consultants have an understanding of local regulations and work to streamline bureaucratic procedures, minimizing delays and obstacles.

Managing risks and uncertainties

Preservation projects can often face risks and uncertainties, including natural disasters, vandalism, and unexpected challenges during construction or restoration. Heritage preservation consultants help stakeholders identify and manage these risks by conducting risk assessments, developing contingency plans, and providing guidance on disaster preparedness. Consultants also assist in building resilience and adapting preservation strategies to changing circumstances.

Case Studies

Preservation of historic city centers

Heritage preservation consulting has been instrumental in the preservation of historic city centers around the world. Consultants work with local governments, businesses, and communities to develop preservation plans, enhance infrastructure, and protect the unique character of these urban areas. Through careful planning and implementation, historic city centers are revitalized and preserved for future generations to enjoy.

Restoration of iconic landmarks

Heritage preservation consultants have played a crucial role in restoring and preserving iconic landmarks, such as ancient temples, castles, and monuments. They collaborate with architects, engineers, and experts in restoration techniques to meticulously restore these landmarks to their former glory. The restoration efforts not only preserve the historical and architectural significance of these landmarks but also contribute to tourism and local pride.

Adaptive reuse of heritage buildings

In many cases, heritage buildings that have lost their original function are repurposed through adaptive reuse projects. Heritage preservation consultants work with stakeholders to identify appropriate new uses for these buildings, while respecting their historical and architectural integrity. This can include converting a former factory into a museum or transforming an old school into residential units. Adaptive reuse projects breathe new life into heritage buildings, ensuring their continued relevance and sustainability.

On the multilateral stage, ASEAN invited coup leaders to a special summit on the situation in Myanmar, from which the NUG was excluded. It is worth noting that General Min Aung Hlaing was not seated as Head of State, but as Commander in Chief of the armed forces.  ASEAN has been instrumental in the past in facilitating changes of direction in Myanmar, for example, facilitating aid flows after Cyclone Nargis in 2008, and repatriating non-Kaman Muslims after Operation Pyi Thaya in 1992. However, despite its potential catalytic influence, ASEAN is restrained by member states with their own authoritarian tendencies and domestic political issues. Additionally, their disagreement over the non-Kaman Muslim issues has rendered them less cohesive than usual. It is thus unlikely ASEAN will act against the Tatmadaw with sanctions or other measures. Similarly, the vetoing power asserted by China and Russia in the UN Security Council prevents the possibility of international military intervention, and the US, UK, and other European powers will not act unilaterally in Myanmar.

At the international governance level, NUG maintains Myanmar’s representation at the UN in New York, and CRPH represents Myanmar at the Inter-Parliamentary Union. UN Specialised Agencies appear to be refusing to accept the accreditation of the Myanmar regime in its assemblies, and Myanmar’s seat stayed empty during the recent World Health Assembly. And, lest you think that developing countries are simply more prone to natural disasters, North America (and the United States especially) is the most disaster-prone region in the world.

Why, then, do developing countries experience so much more loss of life in natural disasters? The answers are many, and vary by the type of disaster. In general, though, poor and weakly governed states suffer from the following problems:

  • Less effective advanced warning.
  • Illiteracy and lower levels of education.
  • Less sturdy buildings and infrastructure.
  • Less effective land use planning.
  • Slower and less effective disaster recovery.
  • In some cases, an unwillingness to accept international assistance, as with the case of Myanmar after Cyclone Nargis in 2008, and North Korea during various episodes of famine.

On a positive note, some developing countries are dramatically improving their disaster preparedness and response. Chile, for example, sustained relatively few casualties after a massive 8.8 magnitude earthquake in  February 2010. Even though major population centers were affected, only about 500 deaths were reported. Progress is possible.

People leave their home countries and seek better lives in foreign countries due to a variety of push and pull factors. Their legal status in the destination countries rests within the government’s decision on whether to grant them refugee status or not. Many also leave for economic reasons, travelling to destination countries with a perceived better economic opportunities and a better standard of living.

Another reinteresting factor that is increasingly driving migration today is climate change. More than ever before, scarcity of resources and extreme weather patterns are causing large-scale human migration, creating climate refugees. These are people who had to abandon their homes and livelihoods due to the adverse effects of climate change. For example, after Cyclone Nargis in 2008, about 2 million people lost their homes, forcing some to migrate to neighbouring Southeast Asian countries like Indonesia.

Furthermore, climate change is usually not the sole push factor in determining a person’s decision to emigrate, but it plays a big role for populations living in the areas worse affected by climate change. The Importance of Beavers and their Role in the Environment

Beavers are often infamous for their tree-munching activities, but their efficiency in utilizing their environment is truly remarkable. By building dams and altering stream flows, beavers not only create crucial habitats for themselves, but also benefit various other species and surrounding landscapes.

One of the primary benefits of beaver dams is their ability to prevent floods and droughts. By creating small ponds and wetlands, beavers help mitigate the risks of both excessive water flow and water scarcity.

During periods of heavy rain, these incredible structures absorb and hold water, acting as natural sponges and decreasing the chance of flooding downstream. In times of drought, the dams help retain water, ensuring a continued supply in the ecosystem.

In addition to flood and drought prevention, beaver dams have a notable impact on the restoration of wetlands. Wetlands are vital ecosystems that provide numerous ecological services, such as water filtration, carbon sequestration, and wildlife habitat.

Unfortunately, many wetlands have been degraded or lost due to human activities. Beavers, with their dam-building abilities, play a crucial role in restoring and expanding wetland areas.

These dams help retain water, raising the water table and creating the perfect conditions for wetland vegetation to thrive. Moreover, beaver dams serve as natural filters, cleansing water as it flows through them.

Their construction works as a form of natural water treatment, removing impurities and pollutants from the water. This process not only benefits the ecosystem but also humans, as cleaner water supports healthier environments for all living organisms.

How to Celebrate International Beaver Day

Now that we understand the significance of beavers and their impact on the environment, let’s explore some ways to celebrate and support these incredible creatures on International Beaver Day. Outdoor Activities:

– Go on a hike and engage in some dam-spotting.

Many parks and nature reserves have beaver habitats where you can observe their handiwork firsthand. – Spend time near a river or lake known to have beavers.

Be patient and observe quietly, as beavers are shy and sensitive to disturbances. You may be lucky enough to catch a glimpse of these busy creatures in action.

In addition to flood and drought prevention, beaver dams have a notable impact on the restoration of wetlands. Wetlands are vital ecosystems that provide numerous ecological services, such as water filtration, carbon sequestration, and wildlife habitat.

Unfortunately, many wetlands have been degraded or lost due to human activities. Beavers, with their dam-building abilities, play a crucial role in restoring and expanding wetland areas.

These dams help retain water, raising the water table and creating the perfect conditions for wetland vegetation to thrive. Moreover, beaver dams serve as natural filters, cleansing water as it flows through them.

Their construction works as a form of natural water treatment, removing impurities and pollutants from the water. This process not only benefits the ecosystem but also humans, as cleaner water supports healthier environments for all living organisms.
